sections.heading: The Company You Call Once and Keep
body: The system in your basement or on the side of your house has probably been there longer than you remember buying it. Someone installed it, someone has looked at it since, and someone will be called when it finally stops.

It makes sense for those to be the same company. A system that has been installed, serviced and repaired by one outfit has a history, and the people who know that history don't have to start over every time.
That's how we work. We put in the system, we look after it, and we're the ones you call when something goes wrong with it.

sections.heading: When Something Breaks
body: A furnace or air conditioner that has run for fifteen years or more is going to break at some point. What matters then is whether the person looking at it knows what they're looking at.
We troubleshoot and diagnose first, so you hear what failed before you hear what it costs. Often it's one part: an ignitor, a wiring fault, a leak.
Sometimes it's the whole system. A repair that makes sense, we repair. A system that's finished, we'll say so and show you the options.

For air conditioners, we find refrigerant leaks and we're EPA registered and certified. For furnaces, we do carbon monoxide detection, because a furnace that burns gas poorly can put it into the house with no smell.
We service all brands, so you don't have to have bought from us to call us.

sections.heading: Air Quality and Humidity
body: The air in a closed house carries dust, pet dander and whatever your filter misses, and the system moves it through every room several times an hour.
We install filters in a range of sizes, and whole-system filtration that goes on any existing system and removes up to 90% of air contaminants.
Winter heat also dries the air out, which is where the static shocks and cracked lips come from. A humidifier on the furnace puts that moisture back.

sections.heading: When the Old System Is Done
body: Nobody wants to replace a furnace or air conditioner. The signs usually arrive over a few seasons.
The repairs get more frequent, and each one costs more than you hoped.
The unit runs nearly all day and never quite catches up. One room is always the hot one, or the cold one. The energy bill creeps up with nothing else changed.
Parts wear, and old equipment loses efficiency. At some point you are paying to keep a system alive that you would be better off replacing, and the honest answer is to say so.

sections.heading: Repair First, Replace When It Makes Sense
body: We don't start from a new system. We start from a diagnosis, because a failed ignitor or a bad capacitor is a repair, not a replacement.
When the system is old and the failures are piling up, or the fix costs more than the unit is worth, we lay out both numbers side by side. You decide.
If you've been told you need a whole new system and aren't sure, call us for a second look.

sections.heading: What We Install
body: We install new heating units and new air conditioners, and we offer a variety of systems and equipment to fit your budget.
For heat, that means furnaces, unit heaters and electric air handlers. For cooling, it means new air conditioners.

We also install humidification and filtration systems, so the air in the house improves at the same time as the equipment. Whole-system filtration adds to an existing system and removes up to 90% of air contaminants, and a humidifier on the furnace gives moisture back to dry winter air.
We work on homes and businesses, and we handle mechanical system design for both.

sections.heading: Sized to the House, Connected to the Ducts
body: A new unit only works as well as the house around it. A system that is too big turns on and off in short bursts and leaves the air clammy. One that is too small runs all day.
The ducts matter just as much. Leaky or crushed ductwork wastes what the new unit makes, and no unit can fix a room it can't reach.
That's one reason we keep a sheet metal fabrication shop of our own. When a fitting or a duct run has to fit an odd space, we make it to the measurements instead of forcing a stock part close enough.

sections.heading: Why Systems Quit on the Worst Day
body: Heating and cooling systems work hardest when it's coldest or hottest outside. That's when a small problem becomes a failure.
A system also gets quietly worse over the seasons. It takes a little longer to cool the house, or a little longer to start, and you stop noticing.
A clogged filter makes the blower strain. Dirty coils make an air conditioner work harder for less cooling. A loose wire or a worn ignitor holds on until the first hard freeze and then doesn't.
Nobody sees any of it from the living room. A system that ran fine in May can be one cold morning from a no-heat call in November.

sections.heading: What a Seasonal Check Is For
body: A service visit before the season is when a worn part is found while it is still cheap and the weather is still mild.

A good check looks at the filter, because the wrong size or a clogged one chokes airflow. It looks at wiring and connections, where small faults hide. It catches a system that is running poorly before you're depending on it.
It also gives someone who knows your system a chance to look at it before something fails. That's how the wiring fault and the wrong filter in Ted H.'s review were caught.
